cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code directly evaluates script content from DOM elements without sanitization, placing user-controlled input into executable JavaScript context

connection.evidence: DOM element content (elem.text/textContent/innerHTML) flows directly to jQuery.globalEval() which executes JavaScript globally

diff_causality.evidence: This line is an addition that creates the inline script execution path; without it, only external scripts via src attribute would be processed

security_control.evidence: No sanitization of script content before evaluation
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-79 requires neutralization of user-controllable input before it becomes executable script content
existing_controls_checked: Browser same-origin policy only applies to external scripts with src attribute
security_control.deficiency_evidence: Inline script content is evaluated without any validation, sanitization, or encoding, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution

concrete_impact.evidence: Arbitrary JavaScript execution in victim's browser context, enabling session hijacking, DOM manipulation, and other XSS consequences

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, inline script elements from parsed HTML would not be executed, eliminating the XSS vector while preserving external script loading functionality.
supporting_evidence: evalScript function processes script elements extracted from HTML content via jQuery.clean()
jQuery.globalEval executes JavaScript code globally by injecting script elements into DOM head
No sanitization applied to elem.text, elem.textContent, or elem.innerHTML before evaluation
unresolved_facts: Specific entry points where user-controlled HTML reaches jQuery.clean()
Whether input validation occurs before HTML parsing in calling code
review_comment: The added line executes inline script content from DOM elements without sanitization, creating an XSS vulnerability. User-controlled HTML containing script tags is parsed and evaluated via jQuery.globalEval, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution. Sanitize or remove script content before evaluation, or use Content Security Policy to restrict inline script execution.
